images.name: porkbot/api
images.reason: Measured 805 MiB on the current base (the alpine trial measured 721 MiB and is stopped; see the PR that introduced this file). The headroom is one large dependency's worth: a dependency added without looking or a toolchain that leaks into the runtime fails here instead of on a host's disk.

images.name: porkbot/migrate
images.reason: Measured 805 MiB — it carries the same deployed workspace as the api, so it shares the api's ceiling and the same headroom rationale.

images.name: porkbot/worker
images.reason: Measured 601 MiB on the current base (517 MiB in the stopped alpine trial). Same headroom as its siblings: enough for one dependency, not for a toolchain.

images.name: porkbot/backup
images.reason: Measured 572 MiB now that the image is a Node runtime plus the two Postgres clients (1014 MiB when it carried the whole server image for them). The ceiling is far under the old shape, so a return to a server base is a red budget rather than a slow drift.

images.name: porkbot/supervisor
images.reason: Measured 520 MiB on the current base (436 MiB in the stopped alpine trial). Same headroom as its siblings: enough for one dependency, not for a toolchain.

images.name: porkbot/proxy
images.reason: Measured 88 MiB: the pinned Caddy image plus the built SPA in /srv/client. The margin is the client bundle's growth, and it is deliberately tight — the proxy must never come to carry a Node runtime.
